blockers.title: EV-5's exact-byte root list drops one of file 04's five GC-reachability roots — active/provisional generations — and its measures field makes an explicit but incomplete enumeration of what that reachability list adds
blockers.finding: File 04 states the removal obligation twice, at different resolutions, and EV-5 uses both. The generation-property bullet at lines 61-82 reads 'remove and GC cannot delete bytes/state referenced by locks, active processes, retained evidence, rollback slots, or prepared migrations', and EV-5's measures quotes it correctly. The fuller statement is the reachability list at lines 123-139, where 'GC computes reachability from' five bullets: project/operation locks and active generation leases; retained authoritative evidence and custody records; ACTIVE/PROVISIONAL GENERATIONS and rollback slots; prepared migrations and repair state; and binding retention policy/tombstones. EV-5's measures then says 'File 04 reachability also names repair state and binding retention policy/tombstones.' That sentence is an express enumeration of the delta between the two statements, and it is short by one: the reachability list also names active/provisional generations. The consequence lands in the exact-byte intent, which is where it matters. EV-5 retains 'removal records showing a generation remains while any named root holds it (project/operation locks, active generation leases, preview-honest retained-evidence/custody records, rollback slots, prepared migrations) and becomes eligible only when those roots are empty.' Five roots are named; active/provisional generations is not among them, and the word 'provisional' does not occur anywhere in the artifact — I searched it. Binding retention policy/tombstones fares slightly better but is still only named in measures as something file 04 'also names', never carried into the retained root set, so it too cannot be scored from the bytes this member pins.
blockers.failureScenario: Take a migration that has reached prepare but not commit. It has produced a provisional generation. That generation holds no project or operation lock, because no project has selected it yet; it carries no active lease, because no operation is running against it; it is not retained evidence, not a rollback slot, and it is not itself a prepared migration — it is the artifact a prepared migration produced. Under file 04 it is reachable, because active/provisional generations are a root. Under EV-5's enumerated root set it is reachable from nothing, so GC may collect it and the fixture built to this specification records a pass. Then a crash injected at the very next boundary — which the crash-injection class requires at every migration prepare, commit, abort and no-return transition — recovers against a generation whose bytes have been collected. This is not a hypothetical corner: the provisional generation between prepare and commit is precisely the object this harness's own first corpus class exists to stress.
blockers.whyItMatters: EV-5's passProperty is 'A referenced generation is not deleted' and 'Waiver of a referenced deletion is forbidden', and the gate's live waiver is 'every reachable durable transition; no waiver for ambiguous authoritative state'. A root that the specification does not retain is a root the harness cannot score, so the strongest sentence in this member is unenforceable for the one generation class the crash corpus most exposes. Everything else in this candidate is complete to the byte, which is exactly why this gap would be trusted rather than checked.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Enumerate all five file-04 reachability bullets in EV-5's exactByteIntent — adding active/provisional generations, and promoting binding retention policy/tombstones from the measures mention into the retained root set — and correct the measures sentence so its delta enumeration is complete. The repair is additive and touches one member; nothing else in the artifact moves, and the existing honest scoping of the retained-evidence root to DR-124 and of repair state to DR-110/G08 can stay exactly as written.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-two attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject a9d80e79 at 0444, 37858 bytes, unmoved and unedited, with the dispatch pin agreeing and no digest token left unfilled; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 is 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now is 26 of 26 and condition 2 is 4 of 32 NOT MET, both matching what the subject carries. Five of five cited digests reproduce. I want the quality of this candidate on the record separately from the verdict, because it is the strongest harness specification I have measured here. It quotes seven of the eight register cells verbatim, including the assurance-stage and status cells that every earlier sibling skipped and that I raised as an advisory against G07. It decomposes the live evidence cell into five members and the live harness cell into three classes, proves both decompositions by punctuation, and then refuses twenty-one specific invented extras in both directions plus a notCollapsed clause for the reverse error — I could not construct a split or collapse it had not already refused. It reconciles the two sources of the executes limbs correctly, stating that the live file 08 'every' and 'no-return' are not optional additions to naming v6's shorter string. It carries all eight file-04 generation properties to a named home, including routing monotonic trust state out to G08/DR-112 with an express statement that it is not a sixth member, which is the routing an author would most plausibly get wrong. It refuses journal, lock-file, lease-API, solver, filesystem-layout and reviewed-equivalent-of-atomic-rename inventions, keeps the quarantine format reserved, and declines to adopt lifecycle-generation-contract.v2's minted identifiers even though that candidate is D-107-recorded. Its waiverHonesty reads the live 'no waiver for ambiguous authoritative state' as generation-publication authority rather than as a sealed-evidence claim, which is the honest reading and closes the preview attack. The blocker is one member. File 04 states the removal obligation twice: the generation-property bullet, which EV-5 quotes correctly, and the fuller GC-reachability list at lines 123-139, whose five bullets include active/provisional generations. EV-5's measures says 'File 04 reachability also names repair state and binding retention policy/tombstones' — an express enumeration of the delta between the two statements, short by one. The consequence is in the exact-byte intent, which names five roots and not that one; the word 'provisional' occurs nowhere in the artifact. A provisional generation between migration prepare and commit holds no lock, carries no lease, is not retained evidence, is not a rollback slot and is not itself a prepared migration, so under EV-5's enumerated roots it is reachable from nothing and may be collected while the fixture records a pass — and a crash injected at the next boundary, which the first corpus class requires, then recovers against collected bytes. That is the object this harness's own crash corpus most exposes. Binding retention policy/tombstones has the same shape one degree weaker: named in measures, never carried into the retained root set, so equally unscoreable. The repair is additive and touches one member: enumerate all five reachability bullets in EV-5's exactByteIntent and correct the delta sentence. Three advisories, none blocking: OBL-G18-HARNESS-SPEC is coined here with no creating join and booked on a gate row, disclosed plainly and now the second gate in that position; gates2and3Hold is unscoped where DR-107 is plainly the row; and basedOn carries a bare head string plus a duplicated file08Pin in an otherwise exemplary provenance block.
